{{Short description|Mathematic concept}}
{{one source |date=April 2024}}
{{unfocused |date=May 2024}}
In mathematics, the '''''n''-th symmetric power''' of an object ''X'' is the quotient of the ''n''-fold product <math>X^n:=X \times \cdots \times X</math> by the permutation action of the [[symmetric group]] <math>\mathfrak{S}_n</math>.

More precisely, the notion exists at least in the following three areas:
*In [[linear algebra]], the ''n''-th symmetric power of a vector space ''V'' is the vector subspace of the [[symmetric algebra]] of ''V'' consisting of degree-''n'' elements (here the product is a [[tensor product]]).
*In [[algebraic topology]], the ''n''-th symmetric power of a [[topological space]] ''X'' is the [[quotient space (topology)|quotient space]] <math>X^n/\mathfrak{S}_n</math>, as in the beginning of this article.
*In [[algebraic geometry]], a symmetric power is defined in a way similar to that in algebraic topology. For example, if <math>X = \operatorname{Spec}(A)</math> is an [[affine variety]], then the [[GIT quotient]] <math>\operatorname{Spec}((A \otimes_k \dots \otimes_k A)^{\mathfrak{S}_n})</math> is the ''n''-th symmetric power of ''X''.
